message.content:
**Short answer:**  
Yes – you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta, but it’s usually handled by the **Atlanta Police Department** or the **City of Atlanta’s Code Enforcement** office rather than directly by the city council. The council may review complaints or refer them to the appropriate department, but they don’t typically take individual noise reports.

---

## How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta

| Step | What to Do | Where to Go / Who to Call |
|------|------------|---------------------------|
| 1 | **Determine the type of noise** (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs, etc.) | — |
| 2 | **Check the city’s noise ordinance** to see the prohibited hours and decibel limits. | [Noise Ordinance PDF](https://www.atlantaga.gov/sites/default/files/2023-08/Noise%20Ordinance.pdf) |
| 3 | **File the complaint**: you have several options: | |
|   | • **Online portal** (non‑emergency) | https://www.atlantaga.gov/311 |
|   | • **Phone** (non‑emergency) | 311 (for non‑emergency city services) |
|   | • **In person** at the Code Enforcement office | 404‑656‑4000 (or visit the office) |
|   | • **Police** (if the noise is an emergency or you’re in immediate danger) | 911 (for emergencies) or 404‑656‑4000 (for non‑emergency police calls) |
| 4 | **Provide details**: location, time, description of the noise, and any evidence (photos, videos, audio recordings). | — |
| 5 | **Follow up**: you’ll receive a case number. Use it to check status online or call the department. | — |

### Contact Information

| Department | Phone | Online |
|------------|-------|--------|
| **Atlanta Police Department – Non‑Emergency** | 404‑656‑4000 | — |
| **City of Atlanta Code Enforcement** | 404‑656‑4000 | — |
| **311 (City Services)** | 311 | https://www.atlantaga.gov/311 |
| **City Council (for general inquiries)** | 404‑656‑4000 | — |

> **Tip:** If you’re dealing with a recurring issue (e.g., a neighbor’s loud party every weekend), it’s helpful to keep a log of dates, times, and any interactions you’ve had with the police or code enforcement. This documentation can support your complaint if the issue escalates.

---

## Why the City Council Isn’t the First Stop

- **City council members** are elected officials who set policy and budget, not frontline service providers.  
- **Noise complaints** are typically considered a public safety or code‑enforcement matter, so the city’s police or code enforcement departments are the appropriate agencies to investigate and enforce the ordinance.  
- The council may **review complaints** if they become a larger community issue or if residents petition for a change in the ordinance, but they don’t usually process individual reports.

---

### Quick FAQ

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **Can I file a noise complaint online?** | Yes, via the 311 portal. |
| **What if the noise is an emergency?** | Call 911. |
| **Do I need to be a resident to file a complaint?** | No, anyone can file a complaint if they’re affected by the noise. |
| **Will the council take my complaint?** | They may review it if it’s a widespread problem, but the initial response comes from police or code enforcement. |

---

**Bottom line:** If you’re experiencing unwanted noise in Atlanta, start with the Atlanta Police Department or the City’s Code Enforcement office. They’ll investigate and enforce the city’s noise ordinance. The city council can be involved later if the issue escalates or if you’re advocating for policy changes.
